message:
I'm drafting the board paper from our team notes. The notes say:

"Varden 24-month report: per-hour gain held steady at 12.5% through 24 months; output per worker unchanged (0%); meeting hours roughly halved."

Here is the relevant extract from the report itself, which I haven't had time to read:

"Table 1 (24 months, case-processing offices, reduced-hours v control). Output per actual hour, system logs: +8.5% (95% CI 3.4 to 13.8); timesheets: +9.8%. At nine months the corresponding system-log figure was +12.5%. Actual hours worked: -11.0%. Output per FTE: -3.4% (95% CI -8.1 to +1.5). Recurring meeting hours per week: 7.4 to 3.9 (control 7.2 to 7.0)."

Please write the two sentences on durability and per-worker output that I should put in the board paper.
response:
Use the report, not the notes. The notes are wrong on both points: the per-hour gain didn't hold steady at 12.5% (it fell to 8.5%), and output per worker wasn't unchanged (it was −3.4%).

**For the board paper:**

> The per-hour productivity gain proved durable but smaller than early results suggested, falling from 12.5% at nine months to 8.5% at 24 months (95% CI 3.4% to 13.8%, system logs). Because actual hours fell by 11%, output per full-time worker was 3.4% lower than in control offices (95% CI −8.1% to +1.5%), so a small fall in output per worker cannot be ruled out, though the result is also consistent with no change.

**Notes on the wording:**
- I've used the system-log figure (8.5%) rather than timesheets (9.8%), because logged data is more reliable and it's the figure the report leads with.
- The second sentence avoids saying output "fell" outright, since the interval includes zero. It also avoids "no loss of output," which the central estimate doesn't support.
- "Meeting hours roughly halved" is accurate for the reduced-hours offices: 7.4 to 3.9, against barely any change in controls.

It's worth correcting the team notes as well, so the 12.5% and 0% figures don't end up in other papers.
